title: Adaptive Error Scorer - UX grooming and lightweight mockups
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a lightweight UX proposal and grooming notes for an "adaptive error scorer" surface in the Console. Goal is to help engineers and oncall quickly understand and prioritize noisy error classes (timeouts, 5xx, model-internal errors) by combining signal weighting, session context, and a dynamic score so that triage decisions are more proactive and less noisy.

Context and problem statement:
- Current console views list raw failure events (per-request) and heatmaps, but signal volume makes it hard to know which classes of failures actually impact user sessions and SLAs.
- Engineers manually inspect traces to find regressions; repeated manual steps across teams.
- We need a low-friction way to surface the highest-impact error clusters with actionable next steps (replay, pin model fallback, open incident).

High-level product goals:
1) Surface prioritized error clusters (scored) with a single-line summary, representative example, and impact estimate.
2) Link each cluster to quick actions: replay, create a ticket, pin fallback path, scope to deployment/model version.
3) Make scoring explainable: show the top contributing signals (latency, user-visible failures, session aborts, % of requests, change rate).
4) Integrate with existing trace and replay flows (minimal friction).

Primary personas:
- Platform engineer: wants to identify noisy runtime regressions across Dedicated pools quickly.
- SRE oncall: needs to escalate based on impact to SLA and user-facing errors.
- Product engineer: cares about feature regressions (quality drop after a rollout).

Proposed UX surface components:
A. Adaptive Error Scorer list (landing panel)
   - Title row: "Adaptive scorer: prioritized error clusters" with dropdown for time window (15m/1h/24h/7d) and relevant environment filter (hosted, dedicated, private).
   - Each row (cluster card) contains:
     * Score badge (0-100) colored (green/orange/red)
     * Short title: e.g., "Model decode timeouts during long-context streaming"
     * Representative example: collapsed request payload + truncated response snippet or error stackline
     * Impact indicators: approximate affected requests (count), unique sessions, % of route traffic, & change rate vs baseline (▲/▼)
     * Top contributing signals (pill list): latency spikes, KV cache misses, model-err-type, region-specific failures
     * Actions: [Replay] [Open Triage] [Pin fallback] [Create issue]
   - Row click expands an in-place detail pane (no full navigation) showing 3 representative traces with timeline scrubber and mini-logs.

B. Cluster detail pane (expanded)
   - Header with cluster name, score breakdown (list of signals and their weight as percentages).
   - Timeline: stacked micro-chart showing requests, error probability, and model variant rollouts overlay. Example ascii:
     |---requests---|    X   |--error-spike--|
   - Representative traces (1 clickable to open full trace in Investigator)
   - Suggested remediation (auto-synthesized): e.g., "increase sequence truncation to 4096, enable prefix caching for route /summarize" + confidence score.

C. Local ranking controls and user feedback
   - Toggle: score weighting preset (SRE-priority, Product-priority, Latency-first)
   - Thumb up/down feedback per cluster to improve future ranking model

D. Bulk actions and saved queries
   - Checkbox select to take bulk actions (create incident, export traces, assign to owner)
   - Save configured filters as a "triage workspace" (team-specific)

Scoring model (simple explainer for agility)
- Score = weighted sum of normalized signals: user-facing-error-rate, unique-sessions-affected, traffic-fraction, recent-change-magnitude, time-to-recovery-estimate.
- Default weights: user-facing-error-rate: 0.35, unique-sessions: 0.25, traffic-fraction: 0.2, change-magnitude: 0.15, ttr: 0.05.
- Expose these weights in UI via a compact modal for transparency.
- Note: initial implementation should compute score from existing observability streams (console metrics + traces) — no new ingestion pipeline.

Wireframe (text sketch)
- Left column (30%): Filters / saved workspaces / quick links to Investigator and Replay
- Middle column (50%): Scored cluster list, expandable rows
- Right column (20%): Selected cluster detail pane + quick actions

Example cluster row (textified):
[ 82 ]  Model decode timeouts — streaming route /chat/stream  (1245 events, 312 sessions, +360% vs baseline)
Top signals: request-latency, kv-cache-miss, model-5xx
Actions: [Replay] [Pin fallback v1.3-q4] [Open Triage]

Backlog grooming notes (sprint-sized slices):
1) MVP backend: score computation job (re-use metrics pipeline) — 5 dev-days. Outputs: cluster id, score, top signals, sample trace ids.
2) UI list + expand behavior + action stubs — 8 dev-days. Use existing Investigator route and Replay API placeholders.
3) Explainability panel + weights UI — 3 dev-days.
4) Feedback loop (thumb up/down) + telemetry — 2 dev-days.
5) Bulk actions & saved workspace persistence — 5 dev-days.
6) Integrations: auto-suggested remediation (heuristic rules) — 6 dev-days (stretch).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console displays scored clusters for selected environment and time window, with scores updating every 1 minute.
- Clicking Replay opens the existing Replay modal pre-populated with representative trace.
- Score breakdown shows top 3 contributing signals and their relative weights.
- Users can save one triage workspace and load it.

Open questions / risks:
- Cluster stability: how frequently will clusters flip membership? Need smoothing to prevent churn.
- Privacy/regulatory: ensure we don't surface PII in representative payloads for Private deployments. Apply automatic redaction.
- Performance: scoring job must be cheap — avoid dense replay of traces for every scoring run.
- Cross-team ownership: which team owns remediation suggestions (Product vs Infra vs Serving Runtime)?

Related signals and metrics to instrument (engineering asks):
- Per-request: route, model_version, deployment_id, latency_ms, token_count, error_type, user_session_id (hashed)
- Per-cluster: event_count, unique_sessions, baseline_rate, change_pct, mean_latency, p95_latency, estimated_user_impact

Prototype interaction notes (for designer):
- Use card-based rows with subtle elevation change on hover; black/amber/red score badges to be consistent with our console color system.
- Animations: when score rises >30% within 15m, animate a pulse to draw attention (configurable).
- Accessibility: ensure color is not the only channel for severity; include icons and clear text labels.

Next steps / owner assignments:
- (Maya) Draft lightweight API payload for cluster objects and post to #console-triage by EOD Thu.
- (Liam) Spike on score job using metrics pipeline and return sample JSON for UI by next Tue. (Link: Linear CS-402)
- (Priya) Design two micro-interactions (expand pane, replay flow) and upload Figma frames.
- (Diego) Validate privacy/redaction approach for Private deployments with Security.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally narrow: focus on ranking noisy classes rather than replacing Investigator. The surface should be a low-friction entry point for triage.
- Comments and edits welcome inline; prefer to iterate quickly and ship an alpha to a small set of teams.

Scratch ideas (future):
- Auto-assign probable owner using commit/rollout metadata and historical fixers.
- Integrate with Optimize to suggest batching/quantization changes if cost-related errors are correlated.
- Alerting: allow teams to create a rolling alert based on cluster score threshold (not raw error count).

References / links (internal):
- Investigator trace format: confluence:investigator/trace-format
- Replay API: https://api.redwood.ai/docs/replay
- Conversation in Slack: #infra-observability thread ts=1700214000

End of note.
